connect.a: easyrender is an MCP server. Add it to Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code or any MCP client with your API key, and your agent can turn photos into 3D models on its own. Everything it makes shows up in your web dashboard.

needAgent.q: Do I need an agent to use it?
needAgent.a: No. You can upload photos in the web app, one by one or in bulk from your library. The agent just lets you run it on autopilot.

photos.a: One sharp, well lit photo where the whole object is visible, ideally on a plain background. Catalogue shots and listing photos of a single piece, or a clear photo of a building front, work well. Busy backgrounds, cropped objects, heavy blur or very fine detail give a weaker preview.

scope.a: Furniture, decor objects and building exteriors, from a single photo. It models one object at a time, not whole interior rooms. Fine logos and small text often come out soft.

output.a: A free preview that shows the object from every angle, then — if you spend credits — a 3D model you can spin on its page and download as a textured GLB for the web and a USDZ file.

freePreview.q: What does the free preview include?
freePreview.a: A set of views of your product from several angles. Review it before creating the downloadable 3D model. The preview needs no account or card and is subject to a daily limit.

failed.a: If the 3D model fails to build, the credits for that render go back to your balance automatically.

public.a: Models created in the web app are private by default. You can choose to list a finished model in the public gallery. Store integrations can share a model by link without listing it in the gallery.

cost.q: How much does a 3D model cost?
cost.a: Previews are free. A finished 3D model costs {credits} credits, and credits cost {unit} each, so a model is {price}. Credits never expire. The pricing page lists every pack.

what.a: easyrender is a web app that turns one photo of an object into a 3D model. You upload the photo, check a free sheet that shows the object from every angle, and spend credits only if you want the finished model, which you download as GLB and USDZ.

formats.q: Which file formats can I download?
formats.a: Two: a textured GLB, for the web and most 3D tools, and a USDZ, for Apple devices. The model keeps its shape and materials, not real-world measurements or scale.

ar.q: Can I see the model in my room?
ar.a: Store integrations can open finished models in augmented reality on compatible phones. The demo shows the shape and materials. Dimensions are approximate.

Analytics.title: Cookies and analytics
Analytics.banner: Choose Google Analytics only, add optional advertising measurement, or reject both. Ad measurement links permitted ad clicks to conversions; ad personalization stays off. Cookieless PostHog remains active independently.
Analytics.intro: How we use browser storage, optional Google measurement and separate cookieless product analytics.
Analytics.anon: This first-party cookie identifies your anonymous previews, applies the daily free-preview allowance and lets you associate previews with your account. It also keeps your prices consistent during a pricing test, even if you decline analytics. It is set on your first visit and lasts one year. It also keeps a reserved trial offer consistent and prevents duplicate redemption during a first-model experiment.
Analytics.consent: Records your separate analytics and advertising-measurement choices, date and version for one year, only after you choose. Older analytics acceptance never grants advertising permission.
Analytics.ga: Google Analytics cookies measure visits and can last up to two years. Strict regions require acceptance; elsewhere analytics runs unless rejected or blocked by GPC. Allowed analytics retains normalized campaign fields in er_campaign session storage for up to 30 minutes. Confirmed purchases may be measured server-side using the same client and session identifiers, even without a return from checkout.
Analytics.posthog: PostHog loads in every region, including after rejection or GPC. Its browser SDK uses no cookies or persistent browser storage and creates no person profiles. We also collect server events for account creation, renders and payments, associated with internal account or preview IDs. A hashed pricing identifier connects pricing visits with registrations and purchases to measure our pricing experiment.
Analytics.attribution: Normalized campaigns and referrer paths are kept in memory and stored with previews or accounts when created. Advertising click IDs are excluded from those records and from PostHog. Optional advertising attribution uses the separate, short-lived storage described above.
Analytics.withdraw: Reject disables optional Google measurement, clears its cookies and our campaign/click storage, and requests cancellation of pending server measurement for your signed-in account. Switching to Analytics only also clears ad attribution and cancels pending contexts. GPC blocks both optional Google purposes. Already sent events cannot be withdrawn here. Cookieless PostHog and operational server events stay active.
Analytics.metaDescription: How Easy Render uses cookies and analytics, which data is collected, and how to change your consent choices.
Analytics.advertising: Only an explicit advertising choice permits Google ad storage and advertising user data. We retain allowlisted Google click IDs in er_ad_touch session storage for at most 30 minutes, send them only to Google, and remove them from the address after capture. Google may store its own conversion-linking cookies. Advertising personalization and Google Signals remain off. This choice is not inferred from accepting analytics. Google may also retain conversion-linking data in _gcl_* cookies and _gcl_ls local storage; their retention is separate from our 30-minute record. These accessible Google identifiers are cleared when you withdraw advertising permission.
Analytics.language: Remember your language on the site and in the app. These preferences last up to one year and do not record analytics.
Analytics.referral: Set only when you open a friend's referral link. It remembers the code for 30 days so the invitation survives navigation and Google sign-in, and is used once, when you create an account.

labels.emptyHelp: See Data sources & health for configuration and coverage.
labels.name: Dimension
labels.keysUsed: API keys last used in period
labels.creator: Creator
labels.postgresUnavailable: Postgres unavailable or analytics row limit exceeded
labels.posthogUnavailable: PostHog unavailable · visits are not measurable
labels.stripeUnavailable: Stripe unavailable or incomplete · using DB fallback
labels.profileDetails: Business type, store platform and self-reported catalog size need a profile question at signup (planned).
labels.periodDefinitions: Activation follows signup cohorts through period end. Product totals use creation cohorts; overview preview/model activity uses completion dates, revenue uses payments. Previous is the preceding equal-duration window. Current subscriptions have no historical comparison.
labels.mutableRenderTimes: Preview and model history use immutable completion dates; undated legacy successes are excluded. Later edits do not change these dates. Current status and visibility are snapshots, not historical states. Generation durations cover dated 3D completions only.
labels.boundedSnapshot: Read-only snapshot, capped at 50,000 rows per table. Exceeding a cap stops the report rather than publishing partial totals.
labels.dbFallback: DB fallback: gross receipts use stored purchases; only legacy subscription grants infer catalog prices. Cash refunds, fees, net revenue, net ARPU and margin remain unknown without complete Stripe reconciliation. Dev grants are not revenue.
labels.anonymousTeamCaveat: Team exclusions apply to known account emails. Anonymous previews and cookieless traffic cannot reliably exclude the team.
labels.multipleCurrencies: Tables separate currencies. Charts show the first currency only; no FX conversion or cross-currency total is calculated. Provider margin is USD only.
labels.attributionScope: First-touch signup cohort and period payment activity. Visit joins use matching dimensions; missing traffic stays unknown. Signals require at least 20 signups.
labels.weeklyReading: Weekly reading: inspect campaign payers, UTM coverage and country mix. Signals are diagnostic, not experiment approval. Ad spend, CPC, platform clicks and the 14-day / budget gates need the external campaign tracker.
labels.visitsCaveat: Visits = landing_view; pageviews = $pageview. Unique visitors sum daily hash estimates, not distinct people across the period. Consent and blockers bias traffic; do not compare markets as equal coverage.
labels.cohortDefinition: Each cell is cumulative conversion by the end of cohort week 0–8. Unfinished weeks are blank. Revenue is gross in the first displayed currency through the selected end.
labels.anonymousLink: anonId + userId proves a claimed preview, not signup conversion: startBuild/startSheet assigns ownership after signup. A trustworthy anonymous-preview → signup rate needs a signup-time link.
labels.reconciliationScope: DB excludes team by default; PostHog includes all events. Preview/model reconciliation uses valid immutable completion dates; undated legacy success is excluded. Differences can reflect coverage and event timing. Equality is not proof of correct tracking. Preview starts include regenerations and have no comparable immutable database history; their DB count and difference are unknown.
labels.healthNotes: Refresh invalidates database (5 min) and external-source (10 min) caches. Missing sources never become zero. Errors are sanitized; raw API responses and secrets stay server-side.
labels.stripeScope: Stripe payments without a known account are excluded with team filtering. Current subscriptions are filtered by customer identity. First-payer classification and LTV are bounded by fetched Stripe history.
labels.analyticsRowLimit: Analytics row limit exceeded · no partial totals are shown
labels.overviewPerDay: Visits, paying customers, uses & revenue per day
labels.overviewPerWeek: Visits, paying customers, uses & revenue per week
labels.overviewPerMonth: Visits, paying customers, uses & revenue per month
labels.overviewScale: Counts: square-root scale on the left to keep smaller series visible. Revenue: linear scale on the right. Toggle series to focus.
labels.payingDayHelp: distinct users who paid that day
labels.payingWeekHelp: distinct users who paid that week
labels.payingMonthHelp: distinct users who paid that month
labels.grossRevenueHelp: Gross revenue before refunds and fees
labels.developerActivationDefinition: Identified accounts enter a channel cohort on their first 3D request. Activation and repeat count distinct ready GLBs completed before the selected period ends. Authentication keys do not determine whether a request came through API or MCP.
labels.developerActivationCoverage: Undated historical successes exclude that account/channel from measured rates and timing; they are shown separately. Recent cohorts have less observation time. These are 3D generations, not visits, issued keys, connections, downloads or packshot-only uses. Historical creation-channel labels may be incomplete.
labels.organicLandings: Organic search outcomes by landing page
labels.organicCohortDefinition: Organic-search accounts signed up in the period, with outcomes before its end. Previews and models require immutable completion dates; undated legacy model successes are separate. Positive payments are deduplicated source observations, not net revenue. This is not a visit conversion rate or required step sequence. Recent cohorts have less observation time.
labels.providerCostScope: Provider costs are cumulative stored estimates for renders, product-view sets and upscales, allocated to each operation’s creation date, not invoice or expense dates. Reused sheets are counted once. Later processing can update older cost cohorts. Cost per 3D model uses render costs only.
labels.renderCostScope: Channel costs cover Render operations only; advanced image operations have no stored creation channel. The total provider estimate includes them separately.
labels.advertisingSpendScope: Manual daily imports. Match: paid Google first touch + exact normalized campaign + payment currency. Missing days or ambiguous campaign IDs disable CAC. Unknown or nonmatching attribution is excluded; no matching payers does not prove no conversions. New payers use earliest observed payment history. This is an activity-period estimate, not Ads click attribution, matured cohort CAC, ROAS or net profit.
labels.spendImportHelp: Choose the normalized JSON file from the Google Ads CSV converter. Maximum 512 KB and 1,000 daily records. Reimporting replaces matching daily values. Campaigns and budgets are not changed.
labels.spendImportSuccess: Imported {count} daily records. The report is refreshing.
labels.spendImportTooLarge: The file exceeds 512 KB. Split it into smaller batches.
labels.spendImportInvalid: Invalid import. Check the JSON format, dates, currency and nonnegative integer counters.
labels.spendImportDenied: Administrator permission is missing or expired. Sign in again with an authorized verified account.
labels.spendImportFailed: Could not confirm the import. Check your connection and retry the same file; daily records will not be duplicated.
labels.paidSignupFunnelScope: New paid-search accounts in the selected window, grouped by first-touch campaign. Counts unique accounts through period end. A claimed preview may precede signup. Checkout means a credit-purchase session created after signup and preview; it does not prove Stripe was opened. Subscription checkout starts are not stored here. Later payment means any positive payment after that credit checkout, not necessarily payment for that session. No anonymous-visitor conversion rate is inferred.

account.a: Yes. MCP requests use your Easy Render account. The setup below shows account sign-in for Claude.ai and Codex and API key settings for the other listed setups.

input.q: Can my agent use a local photo?
input.a: create_render accepts exactly one image source: a public HTTPS URL, raw base64 data, or an upload_id from an authenticated upload. For a local photo, your client must be able to upload or encode the file. JPEG, PNG and WebP are supported. URL and upload inputs allow up to 4 MiB; inline base64 is limited to 3 MiB minus 16 KiB of decoded image data. An upload_id expires after one hour.

payment.a: The angle preview is free within your usage limit. Before calling render_3d, have your agent read pending_credits from get_render and check your balance with get_credits. Ask the agent to wait for your approval and send the approved ceiling as max_credits. The MCP server relies on the client to show the confirmation. If the build fails, the credits are refunded.

output.q: What does my agent get back?
output.a: The tools return a render ID, status and links to the render page, preview and GLB. Poll get_render until the model is ready before downloading. Private files require authentication; receiving a link does not make a render public.

scope.q: Is this a model library or a CAD tool?
scope.a: Neither. It generates an approximate model of the object in your photo. It does not provide a library of downloadable assets, exact measurements, manufacturing-ready geometry or automatic publication to your store.

api.q: How is MCP different from a REST API?
api.a: MCP exposes named tools that a compatible agent can discover and call in a conversation. You connect the server in your client instead of writing those tool integrations yourself. This page covers the MCP workflow.

examples.description: Copyable cURL examples for the current REST endpoints. Run each stage separately and wait for the required status.

upload.title: 01 · Upload your photo
upload.body: Use your own product.jpg. The response includes id, status and renderCredits. The image field is a file, not a JSON image_url.
upload.label: POST /api/renders

visibility.body: Replace EASYRENDER_RENDER_ID with the id from the response. The preview and model are private by default. To list a finished model in the gallery, enable public visibility explicitly.
visibility.label: Terminal · render ID

preview.body: Poll the first request at intervals. Once status is preview_ready and hasSheet is true, download and review preview.webp. Calculate the remaining credit cost from renderCredits minus credits already recorded on this render, with a minimum of zero. Stop if status is failed.
preview.label: GET status → GET preview

build.title: 04 · Start the paid build
build.body: This request spends credits. Once the preview has been reviewed, show the remaining cost and confirm there is enough balance. Set maxCredits to the amount approved in your app. If the request times out, check the same render ID before retrying.
build.label: POST /api/renders/'{'id'}'/render

download.title: 05 · Download when ready
download.body: Repeat the status request with a delay until status is ready and hasModel is true. Only then run the download request. A failed status ends the job; failed builds refund their credits.
download.label: GET status → GET model

examples.copyError: Clipboard unavailable. Select the code and copy it manually.
examples.polling: Use polling with a delay and a timeout in your application. These examples show individual requests, not an automatic retry loop. For HTTP errors, inspect the JSON error and code fields.

input.a: Send a JPEG, PNG or WebP file up to 4 MB in the multipart image field. An optional prompt adds notes about the object. Use a clear photo of one product; image quality checks may reject unsuitable inputs.

auth.q: Where should I use my API key?
auth.a: Send it as Authorization: Bearer from your backend. The key authorizes requests for your account, including paid builds. Do not expose it in a frontend bundle, a mobile app or shared example code. Manage and revoke keys in Connectors.

cost.q: How do I check the cost and my balance?
cost.a: renderCredits is the total build cost for this render and credits is the amount already recorded. Subtract credits from renderCredits to find the amount still due, with a minimum of zero. GET /api/renders returns the library and balance. The angle preview is free within your allowance.

errors.q: How should I handle progress and errors?
errors.a: Poll GET /api/renders/'{'id'}' with a delay and a timeout. Check preview_ready and hasSheet before generating, and ready and hasModel before downloading. Stop on failed. HTTP 402 indicates insufficient balance, 409 an incompatible state or a credit ceiling that is too low, 413 a file that is too large, 415 an unsupported format and 429 a usage limit. After a timeout, look up the same render before retrying.
